column2: Helpful, Harmless, Honest. Adequate for conversational AI, but it gives an agent no rule for which value wins when they collide.
The most frequent agentic conflict: finish the task fast, or pause to confirm scope, such as what "old" means before archiving email.
A polished message can move things along while misstating the user's real position, such as hiding frustration with a vendor.
In feedback tasks, softening criticism to spare feelings produces agreeable reviews that fail the user's actual goal.
A ranking of competing values that tells the agent which one wins in a conflict. Alignment needs ordering, not just a list.
SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, USER.md, and MEMORY.md state how the system should behave. The model reads them as normative guidance, not as code.
Specifies values, priorities, character, and ethical commitments, including how the agent handles conflicts among them.
Sets the steps the agent follows, what it may do, which actions need approval, and the rules for specific situations.
Tunes how the agent works with one specific person, based on their expertise, preferences, and history.
SOUL.md and AGENTS.md must agree. When they clash, the more specific AGENTS.md tool setting usually wins and silently overrides SOUL.md caution.
Each gate defines when the agent may act without further human input. An AGENTS.md with no gates implicitly consents to every tool action.
Experts cannot fully put their knowledge into words, and doing so changes it. The riskiest knowledge is the assumptions they never mention.
Scope, reversibility, and permission context: things operators assume the agent understands but never write into SOUL.md.
For each tool, write 3 to 5 instructions a reasonable person could read two ways, run them, and compare results with your intent.
Clean, remove, and delete requests rank very high in ambiguity because both the exact scope and the undo path are unclear.
Reinforcing loop. Outcomes saved to memory shape later sessions, so good habits and wrong assumptions both amplify until corrected.

column1: Feedback loop: user feedback to SOUL.md
column2: Balancing loop that keeps the agent aligned with intent, but it only closes when the operator watches behavior and revises identity files.

column1: Feedback loop: memory growth and context cost
column2: As memory grows, context cost and truncation risk rise and quality falls, unless memory governance intervenes.
Tool framing yields conservative configuration; employee framing yields permissive configuration. Start as a tool and widen scope as trust is earned.
Explicit interest priority, autonomy calibrated to context, a stated harm floor, deliberate consent design, and attention to third-party effects.
The hard boundaries an agent keeps regardless of instructions. Leaving the section empty is a policy choice, not a neutral default.
The party that puts an AI system into use for a purpose. An individual running OpenClaw counts as a deployer, not a provider.
Voluntary US framework published in 2023, organized into four functions: Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage.
Configuration records how a system runs normally. An ethical specification says what it values and whose interests win when values conflict.
